notes.fact: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh. It was the third night running with emergency alerts in the Saudi capital.
AFP reports the Houthis said on X they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh. The coalition says it destroyed three missiles heading for the capital.
A Malaysian outlet carrying AFP also reports Houthi strikes on Riyadh on Saturday, following the coalition's Hodeida operation. This shows the story is covered across Asia.
The coalition says its strikes on Hodeidah port hit smuggling and weapons-transport capabilities. It also reports hits on missile and drone sites and a supply depot in Sanaa.
A Houthi missile damaged the Riyadh tower housing Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund. Saudi civil defence says no one was hurt, and the financial district was closed to visitors.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Riyadh PIF tower

notes.fact: The Houthis threatened Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports and told airlines Saudi airspace is unsafe. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the Houthi claims of hits on other sites.
notes.event: Houthi threats to Saudi ports and airspace

notes.fact: Zelensky says Russia fired 110 missiles overnight and Ukraine intercepted 79, none of the 27 ballistic ones. At least eight people were killed, according to Zelensky.

Ukraine's air force, per Interfax-Ukraine's summary, reports 82 of 84 cruise and ballistic missiles and 380 drones shot down. This differs from Zelensky's tally of 110 missiles, so counts are not reconciled.
Kyiv authorities say at least seven people died in the capital. Russian strikes also damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies and three Kyiv bridges.

French-language coverage in Spanish from France 24 says the attack followed Putin's vow of a painful response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimea bridge. It also reports blackouts and three damaged Kyiv bridges.

Ukrainian officials say a ballistic and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih killed a seven-year-old boy and a paramedic, and injured dozens. Kyiv Independent counts 83 injured across Ukraine over the past day.
France's foreign minister asked for a UN Security Council meeting after strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv. The EU says it will summon Russia's ambassador.
notes.event: Embassy damage and UN Security Council request

notes.fact: Syria's state news agency reports France condemned the Kyiv strikes and asked for an emergency Security Council session. This is non-Western coverage, though Syria's government is not a party here.
notes.event: Embassy damage and UN Security Council request

notes.fact: Trump told European leaders and Zelensky by phone that Putin wants a deal. Putin said publicly he is open to Europeans joining peace talks.
The Washington Post reports Moscow rules out talks on limited ceasefires and threatens retaliation for Ukrainian strikes, even as Trump says Putin wants peace.
Il Sole 24 Ore, citing the Financial Times, says Trump told Europeans and Ukrainians he wants a peace deal by early January.
One missile fell about 35 km from where European troops were exercising for a possible postwar Ukraine mission. The exercise began Nov 9. Tusk linked the timing to it.
Iran's state media says the IRGC shot down a US MQ-9 over Hormuz with a new air-defence system, its 58th. No US confirmation is given.
An Afghan outlet notes the claim is unverified and the US military has not confirmed it. It also recalls a similar IRGC claim on Nov 4, the 56th.
Al Jazeera, via a Kashmir outlet, says the downing came days after direct US-Iran tit-for-tat strikes and amid rising Iranian attacks on ships in Hormuz.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum in June, but it was never fully implemented over navigation rights in Hormuz. Attacks have resumed periodically since July.
notes.event: US-Iran direct strikes and diplomacy status

notes.fact: A maritime agency cited by The New Arab says one outbound tanker was hit on the stern by an unknown projectile and another in its engine room. No casualties reported.
Iran's army says its drones targeted US missile launchers and Patriot systems at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base, and it downed an MQ-9 east of Hormuz. Unverified.
notes.event: Iranian drone claim on Kuwait base

notes.fact: Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran's seven conditions must be met to reopen Hormuz, including ending the war and lifting sanctions and the naval blockade, though he called the timetable flexible.
AFRICOM says it carried out airstrikes on Nov 17 near Yaaq Shiniile, about 40 km northwest of Kismayo, in coordination with Somalia's government.
AFRICOM reported strikes between Nov 13 and 15 at three sites: near Leego, Yora Lafagari and Jamaame. It also reported a Nov 12 strike near Leego.
Amnesty says nine RSF drone strikes in and around El Obeid killed 37 civilians and injured 10 between June and August 2026. It found no military targets nearby.
notes.event: Amnesty report on El Obeid drone strikes

notes.fact: Sudan Tribune reports the same findings, noting UN rights office data of at least 1,120 civilians killed by drones in the first half of 2026.
notes.event: Amnesty report on El Obeid drone strikes

notes.fact: The hospital's CEO says outside specialists confirmed a cyber incident that began Nov 8, and federal authorities were told. Major elective surgeries and outpatient lab and radiology work are cancelled until Nov 30.
A blog roundup says Chase disclosed a cyberattack on third-party vendors with possible exposure of marketing data. The bank says no service disruption and no link to its earlier outage.

A review through Nov 18 finds no evidence the FAA, Microsoft, Chase, Apple and NSA outages were one coordinated attack. Operators gave technical or maintenance explanations; FAA air traffic resumed Nov 13.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new US outages not attributed
notes.event: November US outages and cyber attribution

notes.fact: A legal-analysis blog says the Director of National Intelligence stated on Nov 17 that intelligence agencies saw no signs of a coordinated or state-sponsored cyberattack behind the outages.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new US outages not attributed
notes.event: November US outages and cyber attribution

notes.fact: Silobreaker says US agencies warned in April that Iran-affiliated actors accessed controllers in water, energy and municipal systems. A late-July FBI warning described pressure loss and flooding in some cases; no supply collapse reported.
notes.event: Iran-linked intrusions into water and energy controllers

notes.fact: The FBI's 2026 alerts page lists a joint FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE advisory on Iranian-affiliated actors exploiting internet-connected Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers across US critical infrastructure. Same equipment is used in the US.
notes.event: CISA/FBI advisory on Iranian PLC exploitation

notes.fact: CISA, FBI, NSA and partners say China-based Integrity Tech enables actors targeting critical infrastructure with botnets and VPN infrastructure. The CISA release is dated Oct 8, earlier than the Nov 9 date in the tracker.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Integrity Technology Group

notes.fact: A Health Management Academy analysis finds clinical systems stayed down a median 15 days in 23 hospital attacks with known restoration dates. The longest lasted 41 days.
A US cyber-incident tracker lists a November cyber incident at Ridgecrest Regional Hospital in California, alongside the Monadnock hospital incident in New Hampshire. No attacker is named.

Slay News says federal authorities are investigating refrigeration failures at military bases and that no link to the European supermarket fridge hacks is established. Low-reliability outlet; date of failures given as August.
notes.event: Refrigeration failures at US military bases

notes.fact: PBS says there is no evidence for viral claims of a 90-day US blackout starting Nov 17. DHS Secretary Mullin said Americans need not stockpile for power, water or food disruption.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new US outages not attributed

notes.fact: A mirror of CISA alerts lists a Nov 17 notice urging immediate patching of a critical Java vulnerability, plus actively exploited zero-days added to the KEV catalog. Not the CISA page itself.
